Title:HEAD I - MINISTRY OF COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, YOUTH AND SPORTS
MPs Speaking:Assoc. Prof. Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim;Dr Ahmad Mohd Magad (Pasir Ris-Punggol);Dr Fatimah Lateef;Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar);Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman;Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang);Mdm Cynthia Phua;Mdm Halimah Yacob;Miss Penny Low (Pasir Ris-Punggol);Mr Abdullah Tarmugi;Mr Ang Mong Seng (Hong Kah);Mr Calvin Cheng (Nominated Member);Mr Christopher de Souza;Mr Matthias Yao Chih;Mr Michael Palmer (Pasir Ris-Punggol);Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade);Mr Viswa Sadasivan;Mr Wee Siew Kim (Ang Mo Kio);Mr Zainudin Nordin (Bishan-Toa Payoh);Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Hong Kah);Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng;Ms Ellen Lee (Sembawang);Ms Joscelin Yeo (Nominated Member);The Minister for Community Development, Youth and Sports (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan);The Minister for National Development (Mr Mah Bow Tan);The Minister of State for Community Development, Youth and Sports (Mrs Yu-Foo Yee Shoon);The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Community Development, Youth and Sports (Mr Teo Ser Luck);The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower and Minister for Health (Mr Hawazi Daipi)

Column No : 2981

 

Adoption

 

     Mr Ang Mong Seng (Hong Kah) (In Mandarin): [For vernacular speech, please refer to Appendix A*.] The Government provides various incentives schemes for babies to encourage Singaporeans to have more children. The schemes have yet to achieve its target. Last year, our TFR dropped again at 1.23%.  One of the key reasons is that young couples who want to have children cannot conceive for various reasons. The only way to have children for these couples is adoption so as to fulfil their desire to raise children.

 

     "The Well Being of Singaporeans", a book by NUS Business School,  has pointed out that  70% of Singaporeans would consider adoption to enjoy a family life. I would like to ask the Minister, during the last three years, how many children were adopted and among them how many were born locally and how many were from other countries.

 

     Current adoption procedures are very complicated, resulting in long waiting time.   To speed up the process, I suggest we simplify the procedures to cut down the waiting time. We can appoint more agencies to handle adoption cases involving children from China.  I would also like the Minister to review and relax adoption polices to facilitate childless couples to adopt children more quickly and easily,  and to allow couples with the means to adopt more than one child.

 

     According to a Zaobao article in one United Nations report, there were 96 million Asian females who 'disappeared'.  In China and India, 85 million females 'disappeared' due to abortion, infanticide or lack of care.

 

     If there are good adoption agreements and systems between countries, these babies can be saved. This will make a positive impact on countries with a low birth rate.  Please consider my suggestions.
